current_example.title: Example: Finding Streamlines of Vector Fields

q-162494.name: Question 1
q-162494.problem: Construct the vector field that has the stream function $ψ(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y-x.$
q-162494.worked_solution:
A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if the following equations hold:

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}
$$

Computing the partial derivatives of the function $ψ(x,y),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =\frac{∂ψ}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y-x) \\  & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y, \\ Q & =-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x} \\  & =-\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y-x) \\  & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector field with the stream function $ψ(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y-x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y) & =P\,i+Q\,j \\  & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,i+(-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y+1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Construct the vector field that has the stream function ψ(x,y)=excos⁡y−x.

a
F(x,y)=−exsin⁡yi+(−excos⁡y+1)j
b
F(x,y)=excos⁡yi−eycos⁡xj
c
F(x,y)=sin⁡yi+(excos⁡y+1)j
d
F(x,y)=excos⁡yi+(exsin⁡y−1)j
e
F(x,y)=exsin⁡yi−(cos⁡y+1)j
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A function ψ(x,y) is a stream function of the vector field F=Pi+Qj if the following equations hold:

P=∂ψ∂y,Q=−∂ψ∂x

Computing the partial derivatives of the function ψ(x,y), we have

P=∂ψ∂y=∂∂y(excos⁡y−x)=−exsin⁡y,Q=−∂ψ∂x=−∂∂x(excos⁡y−x)=−excos⁡y+1.

Therefore, the vector field with the stream function ψ(x,y)=excos⁡y−x is

F(x,y)=Pi+Qj=−exsin⁡yi+(−excos⁡y+1)j.

q-162492.problem: Construct the vector field that has the stream function $ψ(x,y)={x}^{3}-3x{y}^{2}.$
q-162492.worked_solution:
A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if the following equations hold:

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}
$$

Computing the partial derivatives of the function $ψ(x,y),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =\frac{∂ψ}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}-3x{y}^{2}) \\  & =-6xy, \\ Q & =-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x} \\  & =-\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}-3x{y}^{2}) \\  & =-3{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector field with the stream function $ψ(x,y)={x}^{3}-3x{y}^{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y) & =P\,i+Q\,j \\  & =-6xy\,i-(3{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2})\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

A function ψ(x,y) is a stream function of the vector field F=Pi+Qj if the following equations hold:

P=∂ψ∂y,Q=−∂ψ∂x

Computing the partial derivatives of the function ψ(x,y), we have

P=∂ψ∂y=∂∂y(x3−3xy2)=−6xy,Q=−∂ψ∂x=−∂∂x(x3−3xy2)=−3x2+3y2.

Therefore, the vector field with the stream function ψ(x,y)=x3−3xy2 is

F(x,y)=Pi+Qj=−6xyi−(3x2−3y2)j.

q-162510.name: Question 3
q-162510.problem: Construct the vector field that has the stream function $ψ(x,y)={x}^{2}{e}^{1-y}.$
q-162510.worked_solution:
A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if the following equations hold:

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}
$$

Computing the partial derivatives of the function $ψ(x,y),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =\frac{∂ψ}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{e}^{1-y}) \\  & =-{x}^{2}{e}^{1-y}, \\ Q & =-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x} \\  & =-\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{1-y}) \\  & =-2x{e}^{1-y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector field with the stream function $ψ(x,y)={x}^{2}{e}^{1-y}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y) & =P\,i+Q\,j \\  & =-{x}^{2}{e}^{1-y}\,i-2x{e}^{1-y}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

Construct the vector field that has the stream function ψ(x,y)=x2e1−y.

a
F(x,y)=−xe1−yi−2x2e1−yj
b
F(x,y)=−xe1−yi−2ye1−yj
c
F(x,y)=−2e1−yi−2xe−yj
d
F(x,y)=−x2e1−yi−2xe1−yj
e
F(x,y)=−e1−yi−x2e1−yj
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A function ψ(x,y) is a stream function of the vector field F=Pi+Qj if the following equations hold:

P=∂ψ∂y,Q=−∂ψ∂x

Computing the partial derivatives of the function ψ(x,y), we have

P=∂ψ∂y=∂∂y(x2e1−y)=−x2e1−y,Q=−∂ψ∂x=−∂∂x(x2e1−y)=−2xe1−y.

Therefore, the vector field with the stream function ψ(x,y)=x2e1−y is

F(x,y)=Pi+Qj=−x2e1−yi−2xe1−yj.

q-162514.problem: Construct the vector field that has the stream function $ψ(x,y)={y}^{2}{e}^{xy}+{x}^{2}.$
q-162514.worked_solution:
A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if the following equations hold:

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}
$$

Computing the partial derivatives of the function $ψ(x,y),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =\frac{∂ψ}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}{e}^{xy}+{x}^{2}) \\  & =2y{e}^{xy}+{y}^{2}x{e}^{xy} \\  & =y{e}^{xy}(2+yx), \\ Q & =-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x} \\  & =-\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}{e}^{xy}+{x}^{2}) \\  & =-({y}^{3}{e}^{xy}+2x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector field with the stream function $ψ(x,y)={y}^{2}{e}^{xy}+{x}^{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y) & =P\,i+Q\,j \\  & =y{e}^{xy}(2+yx)\,i-({y}^{3}{e}^{xy}+2x)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Construct the vector field that has the stream function ψ(x,y)=y2exy+x2.

a
F(x,y)=xexy(2+y)i−(y2exy+2x)j
b
F(x,y)=yexy(2+yx)i−(y3exy+2x)j
c
F(x,y)=xexy(2+yx)i−(yxexy+2x)j
d

e

Submit

EXPLANATION

A function ψ(x,y) is a stream function of the vector field F=Pi+Qj if the following equations hold:

P=∂ψ∂y,Q=−∂ψ∂x

Computing the partial derivatives of the function ψ(x,y), we have

P=∂ψ∂y=∂∂y(y2exy+x2)=2yexy+y2xexy=yexy(2+yx),Q=−∂ψ∂x=−∂∂x(y2exy+x2)=−(y3exy+2x).

Therefore, the vector field with the stream function ψ(x,y)=y2exy+x2 is

F(x,y)=Pi+Qj=yexy(2+yx)i−(y3exy+2x)j.

q-162493.name: Question 5
q-162493.problem: Construct the vector field that has the stream function $ψ(x,y)={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}+x.$
q-162493.worked_solution:
A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if the following equations hold:

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}
$$

Computing the partial derivatives of the function $ψ(x,y),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =\frac{∂ψ}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}-{x}^{2}+x) \\  & =2y, \\ Q & =-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x} \\  & =-\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}-{x}^{2}+x) \\  & =2x-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector field with the stream function $ψ(x,y)={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}+x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y) & =P\,i+Q\,j \\  & =2y\,i+(2x-1)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

q-162493.html:
Question 5
?

Construct the vector field that has the stream function ψ(x,y)=y2−x2+x.

a
F(x,y)=y2i+(x2−x)j
b
F(x,y)=(2y+x)i+2xj
c
F(x,y)=(−2x+1)i+2yj
d
F(x,y)=(y+1)i−x2j
e
F(x,y)=2yi+(2x−1)j
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A function ψ(x,y) is a stream function of the vector field F=Pi+Qj if the following equations hold:

P=∂ψ∂y,Q=−∂ψ∂x

Computing the partial derivatives of the function ψ(x,y), we have

P=∂ψ∂y=∂∂y(y2−x2+x)=2y,Q=−∂ψ∂x=−∂∂x(y2−x2+x)=2x−1.

Therefore, the vector field with the stream function ψ(x,y)=y2−x2+x is

F(x,y)=Pi+Qj=2yi+(2x−1)j.

q-162614.name: Question 6
q-162614.problem:
Which of the following vector fields have a stream function?

I. $F(x,y)={x}^{2}\,i-xy\,j$

II. $F(x,y)=({x}^{2}-2xy)\,i+({y}^{2}-2xy)\,j$

III. $F(x,y)={e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3y)\,i-{e}^{3x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3y)\,j$
q-162614.worked_solution:
A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each vector field.

- Vector field I doesn't have a stream function. The partial derivatives are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=2x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=2x+(-x)\ne 0.
$$

- Vector field II has a stream function. Indeed, the partial derivatives are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=2x-2y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =2y-2x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=(2x-2y)+(2y-2x)=0.
$$

- Vector field III does have a stream function. Indeed, the partial derivatives are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=3{e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3y),\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-3{e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3y).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=3{e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3y)+(-3{e}^{3x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3y))=0.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

Note that $F(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,i-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j$ is a vector field with simply connected domain $D={R}^{2},$ where $P(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ and $Q(x,y)=-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $F$ has a stream function, since

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y+(-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=0.
$$

Next, we find a stream function. A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if 

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\frac{∂ψ}{∂y}={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y,\,\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y.
$$

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

$$

q-162518.html:
Question 11
?

Which of the following is a stream function for the vector field F(x,y)=excos⁡yi−exsin⁡yj?

a
ψ(x,y)=excos⁡xy
b
ψ(x,y)=exsin⁡y
c
ψ(x,y)=excos⁡y
d
ψ(x,y)=exsin⁡ycos⁡y
e
ψ(x,y)=exsin⁡xy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A vector field F=Pi+Qj with a simply connected domain D⊆R2 has a stream function ψ(x,y) if and only if ∂P∂x+∂Q∂y=0.

Note that F(x,y)=excos⁡yi−exsin⁡yj is a vector field with simply connected domain D=R2, where P(x,y)=excos⁡y and Q(x,y)=−exsin⁡y. Computing the partial derivatives, we have

∂P∂x=excos⁡y,∂Q∂y=−excos⁡y.

Hence, F has a stream function, since

∂P∂x+∂Q∂y=excos⁡y+(−excos⁡y)=0.

Next, we find a stream function. A function ψ(x,y) is a stream function of the vector field F=Pi+Qj if

P=∂ψ∂y,Q=−∂ψ∂x.

In our case, we have

∂ψ∂y=excos⁡y,∂ψ∂x=exsin⁡y.

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

ψ(x,y)=exsin⁡y+f(x),ψ(x,y)=exsin⁡y+g(y)

where f and g are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting f=g=0, we have

ψ(x,y)=exsin⁡y.

q-161437.problem:
Which of the following is a stream function for the vector field
$F(x,y)=(1-2xy)\,i-{y}^{2}\,j?$
q-161437.worked_solution:
A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

Note that $F(x,y)=(1-2xy)\,i-{y}^{2}\,j$ is a vector field with simply connected domain $D={R}^{2},$ where $P(x,y)=1-2xy$ and $Q(x,y)=-{y}^{2}.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=-2y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $F$ has a no stream function, since

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=-2y+(-2y)=-4y\ne 0.
$$

Which of the following is a stream function for the vector field
$F(x,y)={x}^{2}\,i-2xy\,j?$
q-126829.worked_solution:

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=2x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=2x+(-2x)=0.

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}.

$$

$$

$$

where $f$ and $g$ are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting $f=g=0,$ we have

$$

q-162522.name: Question 15
q-162522.problem:
Which of the following is a stream function for the vector field
$F(x,y)=2xy\,i+({y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\,j?$
q-162522.worked_solution:
A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

Note that $F(x,y)=2xy\,i+({y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\,j$ is a vector field with simply connected domain $D={R}^{2},$ where $P(x,y)=2xy$ and $Q(x,y)={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=2y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $F$ has a no stream function, since

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=2y+2y=4y\ne 0.
$$

q-162629.name: Question 16
q-162629.problem: Which of the following represents the streamlines of the vector field $F(x,y)=2xi-2y\,j$ over the domain $D={R}^{2}.$
q-162629.worked_solution:
The streamlines of a vector field are the level curves of its stream function and are tangential to the vector field at every point. 

If $F$ represents the velocity field of a fluid flow, then they show the path traced out by a massless particle as it moves with the flow.

A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

Note that 

$$
F(x,y)=2xi-2y\,j
$$

 is a vector field with simply connected domain $D,$ where $P(x,y)=2x$ and $Q(x,y)=-2y.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=2,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $F$ has a stream function, since

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=2-2=0.
$$

Next, we find a stream function. A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if 

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\frac{∂ψ}{∂y}=2x,\,\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}=2y.
$$

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

$$
ψ(x,y)=2xy+f(x),\,ψ(x,y)=2xy+g(y)
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting $f=g=0,$ we have

$$
ψ(x,y)=2xy.
$$

Finally, we find the level curves of the stream function $ψ(x,y)=2xy$ given by the equations $ψ(x,y)=c.$

Notice that the range of $ψ(x,y)$ is $(-\infty ,\infty ).$ So, we will consider level curves for any value of $c.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}ψ(x,y) & =c \\ 2xy & =c \\ y & =\frac{c}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives us a family of hyperbolas with asymptotes $y=0$ and $x=0$ and, for $c=0,$ the lines $y=0$ and $x=0.$ Therefore, the correct graph (along with the vector field $F$) is as follows:

q-162619.problem: Determine the equation of the streamline that passes through the point $P(0,\pi )$ for the vector field $F(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,i-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j.$
q-162619.worked_solution:
The streamlines of a vector field are the level curves of its stream function and are tangential to the vector field at every point. 

If $F$ represents the velocity field of a fluid flow, then they show the path traced out by a massless particle as it moves with the flow.

A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$

$$

Note that $F(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,i-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j$ is a vector field with simply connected domain $D={R}^{2},$ where $P(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ and $Q(x,y)=-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $F$ has a stream function, since

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y+(-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=0.
$$

Next, we find a stream function. A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if 

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\frac{∂ψ}{∂y}={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y,\,\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y.
$$

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

$$
ψ(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y+f(x),\,ψ(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y+g(y)
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting $f=g=0,$ we have

$$
ψ(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y.
$$

Finally, we find the level curve of the stream function $ψ(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y$ that passes through $P.$
First, we find the value of the stream function at $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}ψ(0,\pi ) & ={e}^{(0)}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the streamline that passes through $P(0,\pi )$ is the $0$-level curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}ψ(x,y) & =0 \\ {e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y & =0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

q-162160.problem: Which of the following represents the streamlines of the vector field $F(x,y)=(\frac{1}{y-{x}^{2}})i+(\frac{2x}{y-{x}^{2}})j$ over the domain $D=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,y>{x}^{2}\}.$
q-162160.worked_solution:
The streamlines of a vector field are the level curves of its stream function and are tangential to the vector field at every point. 

If $F$ represents the velocity field of a fluid flow, then they show the path traced out by a massless particle as it moves with the flow.

A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

Note that 

$$
F(x,y)=(\frac{1}{y-{x}^{2}})i+(\frac{2x}{y-{x}^{2}})j
$$

 is a vector field with simply connected domain $D,$ where $P(x,y)=\frac{1}{y-{x}^{2}}$ and $Q(x,y)=\frac{2x}{y-{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=\frac{2x}{(y-{x}^{2})^{2}},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-\frac{2x}{(y-{x}^{2})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $F$ has a stream function, since

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=\frac{2x}{(y-{x}^{2})^{2}}+(-\frac{2x}{(y-{x}^{2})^{2}})=0.
$$

Next, we find a stream function. A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if 

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\frac{∂ψ}{∂y}=\frac{1}{y-{x}^{2}},\,\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}=-\frac{2x}{y-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

$$
ψ(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(y-{x}^{2})+f(x),\,ψ(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(y-{x}^{2})+g(y)
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting $f=g=0,$ we have

$$
ψ(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(y-{x}^{2}).
$$

Finally, we find the level curves of the stream function $ψ(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(y-{x}^{2})$ given by the equations $ψ(x,y)=c.$

Notice that the range of $ψ(x,y)$ is $(-\infty ,\infty ).$ So, we will consider level curves for any value of $c.$ So, we have:

$$

$$

The equation above gives us a family of parabolas with the vertex at $(0,{e}^{c}).$ Therefore, the correct graph (along with the vector field $F$) is as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=2x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-2x.\end{aligned}

EXPLANATION

The streamlines of a vector field are the level curves of its stream function and are tangential to the vector field at every point.

If F represents the velocity field of a fluid flow, then they show the path traced out by a massless particle as it moves with the flow. .

A vector field F=Pi+Qj with a simply connected domain D⊆R2 has a stream function ψ(x,y) if and only if ∂P∂x+∂Q∂y=0.

Note that F(x,y)=x2i−2xyj is a vector field with simply connected domain D=R2, where P(x,y)=x2 and Q(x,y)=−2xy. Computing the partial derivatives, we have

∂P∂x=2x,∂Q∂y=−2x.

Hence, F has a stream function, since

Next, we find a stream function. A function ψ(x,y) is a stream function of the vector field F=Pi+Qj if

P=∂ψ∂y,Q=−∂ψ∂x.

In our case, we have

∂ψ∂y=x2,∂ψ∂x=2xy.

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

ψ(x,y)=x2y+f(x),ψ(x,y)=x2y+g(y)

where f and g are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting f=g=0, we have

ψ(x,y)=x2y.
